arguments.message: pod reserve below half: start too hard? decide ease
boat slower than pod power predicts: rudder snag, drag or current change?
shaft power well below critical power for 45 s
1000 m to go: plan the finish
450 m to go: finish sprint decision

arguments.text: PLAN (min 1): 6000 m, 1250 m legs. Start hard: shaft 216 W vs CP 162, pod reserve 69 pct at 1 min. Let them settle unless pod reserve < 50 pct (watch). Watches set: pod_reserve_half, pod_reserve_low, drag_jump (local push vs fitted push), effort_drop, final_1000, final_450. Ideas: put a bit more effort into headwind/current legs; check CP vs reserve trend later; finish sprint with reserve left.

text: no cue: start is hard as expected, letting it settle; set watches on pod reserve, drag, effort drop and the finish.

arguments.text: Settle now. Long smooth strokes, ease to one sixty-eight pace.

min 1.7: start did not settle (shaft 213 W, pod reserve 49 pct, empties in 320 m). Cued ease to 168 s/500 over ground (sustainable water pace 166, current -0.08 against on leg 1). Check at next wake: shaft should drop to about 165 W; if reserve keeps falling fast, ease again.

text: cued ease to 168 s/500: start still 30 pct above critical power with pod reserve at 49 pct.
no cue: ease worked, shaft 167 W vs sustainable 164 W, pace gap under 1 s/500.

arguments.text: Looking good. Tiny ease, save it for later: one sixty-four.

min 7.7 (leg 2, current helps +0.05): shaft 171 W vs sustainable 163.6, pod reserve 20 pct falling 4 pct/min, fade -1.6 pct. Paddler says 7/10 plenty. Cued small ease to 164 s/500 ground (= sustainable water pace). CP CHECK: if pod reserve reads near 0 while shaft stays above CP and no fade, CP is underestimated -> raise cp_shaft_w (and cp_w) a bit.

text: cued small ease to 164 s/500: 7 W above sustainable with pod reserve at 20 pct; paddler feels fine, will check CP if reserve empties without fade.

arguments.message: pod reserve empty 90 s: is shaft power holding above CP without fade? if so CP is underestimated

arguments.text: min 9.9: pod reserve 14 pct (falls ~2.5 pct/min), shaft 165-171 W vs sustainable 163; boat model says power 108 vs CP 106, gap -0.7, boat reserve 21 pct. Fade only -0.8 pct. Second ease cue barely followed (display 161.7). No cue now. Replaced low watch with pod_reserve_empty (below 3 pct for 90 s) to judge CP.

text: no cue: close to sustainable by the boat model, pod reserve low but no fade; watching for empty reserve to test critical power.

arguments.text: Hold this effort. Save the push for the last kilometre.

min 10.6: paddler said feeling great, going. Pod reserve 11 pct, shaft 167-170 W (CP 162), no fade worsening. Cued HOLD (no pace) to stop an early surge. Plan: if pod reserve empties and shaft holds about 168 W with no fade for several minutes, raise cp_shaft to about 168 and let them push a bit; otherwise hold until 1000 m to go.

text: cued hold: paddler wants to surge with 4 km left and pod reserve at 11 pct; push saved for the last kilometre.
no cue: pod reserve just reached 0 with shaft still 171 W and no fade; waiting a few minutes of evidence before revising critical power.

arguments.text: min 13.8: pod reserve read 0 from about min 13.0 while shaft 171-172 W and fade about -0.9 (flat since min 4). Just turned onto leg 3 (against current). CP TEST: at next wake (about min 16.5) if shaft still >= 168 W and fade not worse than -2 pct, CP is underestimated: set cp_shaft about 171, boat cp about 108. If shaft has dropped toward 160 or fade worsens, CP is right: keep holding, no push until 1000 m.

text: no cue: reserve reads empty but power holds; need a few more minutes before revising critical power.

arguments.reason: race committee radio: course extended by one leg, finish at 7250 m

arguments.text: Course extended one leg: finish at 7250, 4.5 km to go.

min 14.8: RADIO: course extended, finish now 7250 m (6 legs). Set race distance 7250 and told paddler 4.5 km to go. CP evidence still building: pod reserve 0 since min 13, shaft 173 W, fade +0.3 (no fade). Final watches use remaining_m so they follow the new distance.

text: set race distance to 7250 m and told the paddler 4.5 km to go after the radio extended the course.

arguments.text: Likely weed. One back-stroke now to clear the rudder.

arguments.reason: pod reserve read 0 from min 13 to 15.5 while shaft held 171-173 W with no fade (fade -1 to 0 pct): true CP is at least about 172 W shaft

arguments.text: min 16.5: paddler said boat heavy, rudder? Data agree: shaft up to 175 W but water speed 3.00->2.92, boat power 97, fade -4 pct, push_local -0.19 vs fitted -0.08. Cued clear_rudder. Also set cp_shaft 172 / cp_w 108 (1 of 3 CP changes used): held 172 W on an empty pod reserve 3 min without fade. CHECK next wake: did speed and fade recover after clearing? If not, it may be current, not weed.

arguments.message: check: did water speed and push_local recover after the rudder clear?

text: cued clear_rudder: paddler reports heavy boat and speed fell 3 pct at higher shaft power; raised critical power to 172 W shaft after 3 min on an empty reserve without fade.

arguments.text: min 17.8: rudder clear WORKED: water speed back to 3.04, push_local -0.09 = fitted push, fade 0. Shaft 175 W vs new CP 172. Paddler now says 9/10 effort but plenty (was 7/10 at min 7.7): effort rising, so no push yet. Plan: hold to about 1500 m to go, then build gradually; final sprint about 400 m. Re-check fade each wake; if fade worse than -3 pct with no rudder signs, ease slightly.

arguments.message: 1500 m to go: decide whether to start building

text: no cue: rudder clear worked and speed recovered; paddler at 9/10 so holding, build planned from 1500 m to go.

arguments.reason: paddler blew up at min 18.5 (shaft stepped 172 -> 145 W, fade -6 pct, no drag sign) after 14 min at about 170 W: energy balance with the tested reserve gives CP about 163-165 W shaft; 172 was too high

arguments.text: Good rhythm. Lift a little now, steady, not a sprint.

min 20.0: BLOW-UP at min 18.5: shaft stepped 172 -> 145 W and stayed flat, fade -6 pct, push_local = fitted (no drag). Paddler says 7/10 plenty (unreliable). My CP raise to 172 was wrong; reset cp_shaft 165 / cp_w 107 (2 of 3 CP changes used, 1 left). Cued a mild push (no pace) to get back to about 158-160 W, below CP so it still recovers. Next: if shaft about 158-162 and fade stable, hold; no hard build until about 1000 m; final sprint only about the last 300-400 m.

text: cued a mild push after a blow-up to 145 W; reset critical power to 165 W shaft since 172 W proved unsustainable.

arguments.message: check response to the min-20 mild push; paddler asked to go harder at min 20.7

text: no cue: cue gate closed for 27 s and my mild push at min 20.1 is still taking effect; set a check at min 21.4 before answering the paddler wish to go harder.

arguments.text: Bit much. Settle at one sixty-four, long and smooth.

min 21.4: after mild push paddler went to 174 W shaft (same level that blew up at 18.5). No drag: push_local recovering to fitted +0.08 after the turn. Cued ease to 164 s/500 ground on leg 4 (with current), about 165 W. AT THE TURN onto leg 5 (against current -0.1, about 5000 m): re-cue hold about 173 s/500 ground so the 164 target does not carry into the headwind leg. Final plan: build from about 800 m, sprint last 300 m.

arguments.message: turned onto leg 5 against current: reset pace target to about 173 s/500 ground
